certificate.title: Module 2: Using AI to Communicate Completion

course.description: Use AI as your writing partner. Draft emails, memos, summaries, and stakeholder updates in minutes instead of hours. Learn to control tone, audience, and format — and make AI output sound like you, not like a robot. Build a Finance Communications Writer agent.
learningOutcomes: Apply the methods taught in Module 2: Using AI to Communicate.

modules.description: Why AI is a writing superpower. How it eliminates the blank page problem — and how to solve the "doesn't sound like me" problem.

activities.title: What AI Is Good At: Writing

lessons.content:
If gaining knowledge is AI's first superpower, writing is its second. AI is exceptionally good at generating clear, structured, professional text — fast. It can draft an email in seconds that would take you 15 minutes to write from scratch.

But here's the key: **AI doesn't replace your thinking. It replaces the blank page.**

The hardest part of writing is usually starting — staring at an empty email, figuring out how to structure your thoughts, finding the right tone. AI eliminates that friction. You tell it what you need to communicate, and it gives you a draft. Then you edit, adjust, and make it yours.
lessons.title: What AI Is Good At: Writing

lessons.content:
Think about how you write today. Most professional writing follows this pattern:

1. Think about what you need to say
2. Stare at a blank page
3. Write a rough draft
4. Rewrite it 2-3 times
5. Send it

With AI, the pattern becomes:

1. Think about what you need to say
2. Tell AI what you need
3. Review the draft and edit it
4. Send it

You skip the hardest part — the blank page — and go straight to editing. Editing is almost always faster and easier than writing from scratch. And you still control every word that goes out.
lessons.title: Writing vs. Editing

activities.title: The Tone Problem — And How to Solve It

lessons.content:
The most common complaint about AI-generated writing is: "It doesn't sound like me." That's fair — and fixable.

AI defaults to a certain style. Left to its own devices, it can be too formal, too structured, too AI-sounding. But you can direct it to match your tone:

| You Say | AI Adjusts To |
|---|---|
| "Keep it casual and direct" | Conversational, short sentences |
| "This is going to the CFO — keep it formal and concise" | Executive tone, bottom-line-up-front |
| "Write it like an internal Slack message" | Informal, quick, to the point |
| "Make it warm but professional — this is a client" | Polished but personable |
| "I'm explaining this to someone non-technical" | Simple language, no jargon |

The trick is to tell AI about the **audience** and the **tone** — not just the content. "Write me an email about budget variances" gives you a generic email. "Write me a concise email to my VP of Operations explaining why Q3 spending came in 12% over budget, focusing on the two main drivers, and recommending next steps — keep it direct and action-oriented" gives you something you can actually send.
lessons.title: The Tone Problem — And How to Solve It

lessons.content:
Pick a real communication you need to write — or one you recently wrote that took longer than you wanted. It can be an email, a memo, a Slack message, a summary, or anything else you communicate in your role.

**The default example used throughout this module is:**

> **A variance analysis email** — explaining to business stakeholders why actual spending came in over budget for the quarter.

If you're not sure what to pick, use this default. Otherwise, choose your own scenario and follow along with the same steps.
lessons.title: Choose Your Scenario

modules.title: Context / Theory

modules.description: Hands-on steps. Draft a real communication, iterate on it, try different formats, and make it sound like you.

lessons.content:
Go to one of the platforms below and sign in.

- **ChatGPT** → https://chat.openai.com
- **Claude** → https://claude.ai
- **Grok** → https://grok.com
lessons.title: Step 1: Open an AI Tool

lessons.content:
Give AI the details of what you need to write. Include:
- **What** you're communicating (the content)
- **Who** it's for (the audience)
- **How** it should sound (the tone)

> **Try this (default example):**
> "Draft an email to my VP of Operations. I need to explain that Q3 actual spending came in 12% over budget — $2.4M actual vs. $2.14M budget. The two main drivers were: (1) unplanned contractor costs for the system migration that ran 6 weeks longer than expected, and (2) higher-than-expected travel costs from the three new client implementations. I want to recommend we adjust the Q4 forecast to account for the remaining migration costs and put a cap on travel spend for the rest of the year. Keep it concise, direct, and action-oriented."

Read the draft. Notice how it structured the information, how it opened and closed the email, how it framed the recommendations. You probably wouldn't have written it exactly this way — but it gave you a solid starting point in seconds.
lessons.title: Step 2: Draft a Communication

lessons.content:
Now make it better. Instead of rewriting the whole thing yourself, just tell AI what to change:

| You Say | What Happens |
|---|---|
| "Make it shorter — cut it in half" | AI tightens the language, removes redundancy |
| "The opening is too soft — lead with the numbers" | AI restructures to put the bottom line first |
| "Add a one-line executive summary at the top" | AI adds a summary line |
| "Change the tone — this reads too formal for our culture" | AI adjusts to be more conversational |
| "Can you also include a simple table showing budget vs. actual?" | AI adds a formatted table |
| "Rewrite this as a Slack message instead of an email" | AI adapts the format entirely |

This is the power of conversational AI for writing. You don't have to write a perfect prompt the first time. Just iterate — first draft → feedback → revised draft → feedback → done.
lessons.title: Step 3: Iterate and Refine

lessons.content:
Now try using AI for a completely different type of communication. Pick one or try several:

**Meeting summary:**
> "I just had a meeting about our Q4 close timeline. Here are my rough notes: [paste your notes]. Turn this into a clean meeting summary with action items, owners, and due dates."

**Stakeholder update:**
> "Write a weekly status update for my team's stakeholders. This week we completed the bank reconciliation for all 12 entities, identified a $45K intercompany discrepancy that's being investigated, and started the fixed asset roll-forward. Next week we're focused on completing the IC elimination entries and starting the consolidation. Keep it brief — bullet points."

**Difficult conversation email:**
> "I need to email a vendor to let them know we're not renewing their contract. Be professional and respectful, thank them for their service, and let them know the transition timeline is 60 days. Don't burn the bridge — we might work with them again."

**Explanation for a non-finance audience:**
> "Write a short explanation for our product team about why we need to defer revenue on the new subscription product. They don't have an accounting background — keep it simple and use an analogy if it helps."
lessons.title: Step 4: Try Different Communication Types

activities.title: Step 5: Make It Sound Like You

lessons.content:
Take one of the drafts AI generated and compare it to how you normally write. Ask yourself:
- Would I use these words?
- Is this how I'd structure this?
- Does this match the culture of my team / company?

If something feels off, tell AI:
> "This is good but it's a bit too formal for how we communicate internally. Make it more casual — like how a senior manager would write to their team, not how a consultant would write to a client."

Or:
> "I like the structure but the language is too flowery. I'm more of a 'here's what happened, here's what we're doing about it' kind of writer. Tighten it up."

The more specific you are about your style, the closer AI gets. Over time, if you use a dedicated agent, you can train it to default to your voice.
lessons.title: Step 5: Make It Sound Like You

lessons.content:
You just used AI to draft professional communications. Think about the experience:

- How long would that email have taken you to write from scratch? How long did it take with AI?
- Did AI capture the key points accurately?
- How much editing did you need to do to make it "yours"?
- Were there any parts where AI said something you wouldn't have — in a good way?

One important note: always read the full output before sending anything. AI can occasionally include details that aren't quite right, make assumptions about facts it doesn't have, or use a tone that doesn't fit. The draft is a starting point — your review is the quality control.
lessons.title: Step 6: Reflect

modules.title: Now To Do

modules.description: Every type of finance communication AI can help with — variance emails, audit responses, board narratives, and more.

lessons.content:
- **Email responses:** When you get a question from a business partner that requires a detailed answer — about a journal entry, a variance, a policy — paste their question into AI and ask it to draft your response. You'll reply in 2 minutes instead of 15.

- **Status updates:** Weekly or monthly updates to stakeholders, project sponsors, or leadership. Give AI the bullet points and let it format them into a polished update.

- **Slack and Teams messages:** Even quick internal messages benefit from AI. When you need to explain something complex in a chat, ask AI to help you phrase it concisely.
lessons.title: Day-to-Day Writing

lessons.content:
- **Variance explanations:** Every close cycle, someone has to explain the numbers. Give AI the data points and context, and it drafts the narrative — for management reports, board packs, or flash reports.

- **Meeting notes and action items:** After a meeting, dump your raw notes into AI and ask it to clean them up into a structured summary with action items and owners.

- **Audit responses:** When external auditors ask for explanations of specific treatments or judgments, AI can help you draft clear, well-structured responses.
lessons.title: Reporting and Summaries

lessons.content:
- **Delivering bad news:** Budget overruns, missed deadlines, audit findings. AI can help you frame difficult messages diplomatically while still being direct.

- **Escalation emails:** When you need to escalate an issue — to your manager, a business partner, or a vendor — AI helps you strike the right tone between urgency and professionalism.

- **Policy communications:** Rolling out a new expense policy or changing an approval workflow? AI drafts the announcement in a way that's clear and anticipates questions.
lessons.title: Sensitive Communications

lessons.content:
**Cross-functional:**
- **Translating finance to non-finance:** Explaining revenue recognition to product managers, capital expenditure rules to facilities, or budget constraints to department heads. AI adapts your message to the audience.
- **Executive summaries:** Taking a detailed analysis and condensing it into a one-pager for leadership. AI is great at distilling — give it the long version and ask for the short one.

**Recurring:**
- **Monthly close communications:** The same types of emails and updates go out every close cycle. With AI, you can generate them faster each time — and eventually automate the pattern with a dedicated agent.
- **Board materials narratives:** The written sections that accompany board financial presentations. AI can draft these from your talking points.
lessons.title: Cross-Functional and Recurring Communications

modules.title: Application

modules.description: Optional. Build a Finance Communications Writer agent that knows your role, audiences, and writing style.

activities.title: The Idea: A Writing Agent That Knows Your Style

lessons.content:
In the main exercise, you drafted individual messages by giving AI full context each time. That works for one-off communications. But what if you had an AI that already knows your role, your audience, and your writing style? Instead of explaining context every time, you'd just say "draft me a variance email" and it already knows how you like them.

**What you'll create:** A Finance Communications Writer — an AI assistant that knows your role, your typical audiences, and how you like to write. Ready to draft any professional communication on demand.
lessons.title: The Idea: A Writing Agent That Knows Your Style

activities.title: Option A: Create a Custom GPT in ChatGPT

lessons.content:
1. Go to **https://chat.openai.com** and sign in
2. In the sidebar, click **Explore GPTs** → **Create**
3. **Name:** `Finance Communications Writer`
4. **Instructions:** Paste the following (modify for your role):

```
You are my dedicated communications writer. I work in a finance function and need help drafting professional communications quickly.

My typical audiences include:
- Executive leadership (CFO, VP Finance, CEO)
- Business partners (department heads, project managers)
- My own finance team
- External parties (auditors, vendors, clients)

When I ask you to write something:
- Ask me for key details if I haven't provided enough (audience, purpose, key points, tone)
- Default to concise, direct communication — no fluff
- Structure emails with the bottom line up front (BLUF) when appropriate
- Use plain language — avoid jargon unless the audience is finance
- For numbers, always include context (vs. budget, vs. prior year, % change)
- Adapt your tone to the audience — executive communications should be polished and concise, internal team messages can be more casual
- If I give you rough notes or bullet points, turn them into polished prose

If I say "make it more like me" or "that's not my style," ask me what to change and remember it for next time.
```

5. Click **Save** → Choose **Only me**
lessons.title: Option A: Create a Custom GPT in ChatGPT

activities.title: Option B: Create a Project in Claude

lessons.content:
1. Go to **https://claude.ai** and sign in
2. In the sidebar, click **Projects** → **Create a project**
3. **Name:** `Finance Communications Writer`
4. In the **Project instructions** field, paste the same instructions from Option A
5. Click **Create project**
6. You can now start conversations within this project — Claude will always have your writing preferences loaded
lessons.title: Option B: Create a Project in Claude

activities.title: Option C: Create an Agent in AI Gym

lessons.content:
1. Open the **AI Gym** app and sign in (download at https://aigym.studio/#download if needed)
2. On Home, type: *"Create an agent called Finance Communications Writer in my My Training Portfolio org with these instructions:"* and paste the instructions from Option A
3. The Hub creates it for you. Or go to **Org** → My Training Portfolio → **+ New Agent**

Your communications agent is now part of your training portfolio alongside your research agent from Module 1.
lessons.title: Option C: Create an Agent in AI Gym

lessons.content:
Open a conversation with your **Using AI Series Agent** and update it:

> "I just completed Module 2. I created a Finance Communications Writer agent. I learned how to use AI to draft emails, memos, summaries, and messages — and how to adjust tone and format for different audiences. The biggest takeaway was [your takeaway]."

Your portfolio now has **two working agents**: a research expert and a communications writer.
lessons.title: Build on Your Portfolio

modules.title: Bonus: Going Deeper

modules.description: Key terms introduced in this module, explained in plain language.

lessons.content: The process of refining AI output through back-and-forth conversation. You give feedback, AI revises, you give more feedback, AI revises again. Each round gets you closer to what you want — faster than rewriting it yourself.
lessons.title: Iteration

lessons.content: The style and feel of written communication. AI can adjust its tone based on your direction — formal for executives, casual for internal teams, diplomatic for sensitive topics. The same information can be communicated in very different ways depending on the tone.
lessons.title: Tone

lessons.content: A communication style where you lead with the conclusion or key takeaway before providing supporting details. Common in executive and military communications. Very effective in finance — busy stakeholders want the answer first, then the explanation.
lessons.title: BLUF (Bottom Line Up Front)

lessons.content: The directions you give an agent or project that apply to every conversation. This is what makes a general AI into a specialized one — it already knows its role, your preferences, and how to behave before you even ask your first question.
lessons.title: System Instructions / Custom Instructions

lessons.content: The basic unit AI uses to process text. Roughly, 1 token ≈ ¾ of a word. This matters because AI tools have limits on how much text they can process in a single conversation. For most professional writing tasks, you won't hit these limits — but it's why very long documents sometimes need to be broken into sections.
lessons.title: Token
